subject: Orion MAP - streaming TTFT & latency benchmarking (plan + results)

Subject: MAP: Orion - streaming latency & TTFT benchmarking plan

Hi Maria / Tim,

Thanks again for the call — attached is the initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and the performance benchmarking plan focused on chat/text streaming behavior (TTFT + continuous-stream latency). The goal is to validate production SLOs and close the contract by end of Q2. Summary below: 

High-level objectives:
- Validate TTFT (time-to-first-token) and per-token streaming latency at representative concurrency for Orion's chat workload.
- Provide p50/p95/p99 measurements for TTFT and streaming latency, plus tokens/sec throughput at concurrency levels.
- Identify any tail-latency regressions and mitigation steps (batching, model variant, cache policy).

Success criteria (proposed):
- TTFT p95 <= 300 ms for single-turn short prompts (baseline).
- Per-token streaming p95 <= 30 ms at target concurrency (16 concurrent users).
- No p99 TTFT > 1.2s at production concurrency after mitigations.

Planned test matrix (attached in benchmark-plan.xlsx):
- Model variant: redwood-chat-medium + quantized fallback (mq8_compat).
- Sequence profiles: short prompt (avg 40 tokens), medium (avg 150 tokens).
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 32, 128 parallel chat sessions.
- Metric collection: TTFT, stream per-token latency (first 20 tokens), end-to-end tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, kernel-level traces.

Deliverables and timing:
- Initial run (prelim): 2026-05-25 — internal-only, draft CSV of results.
- Customer review: 2026-05-29 — walkthrough with Orion.
- Final MAP update + mitigation plan: 2026-06-05 — include signed close timeline.

Attachments: ORH_MAP_v0.1.pdf, benchmark-plan.xlsx

Can you confirm the acceptance criteria above and whether the concurrency sweep covers the correct traffic envelope for your pilot?

Best,
Jonas

Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@orionhealth.com>, Tim Keller <tim.keller@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-27T14:38:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP: Orion - streaming latency & TTFT benchmarking plan — preliminary results

Hi all,

We completed the internal benchmarking sweep on 2026-05-26 and attached the raw CSV (streaming-results.csv) plus a short executive summary below. This was run on our Dedicated staging pool (A100s, driver runtime 2.3.1) against the short and medium prompt profiles. Notes: tests used production request routing, KV caching enabled for repeated prefixes, and the redwood-chat-medium model.

Executive findings (short prompts, median-length responses ~60 tokens):
- Concurrency 1:
  - TTFT: p50=72 ms, p95=138 ms, p99=240 ms
  - Streaming per-token latency: p50=9 ms, p95=22 ms, p99=40 ms
  - Throughput: ~95 tokens/sec (single session sustained)
- Concurrency 8:
  - TTFT: p50=85 ms, p95=210 ms, p99=410 ms
  - Streaming per-token latency: p50=11 ms, p95=28 ms, p99=60 ms
  - Aggregate throughput: ~720 tokens/sec (8 sessions combined)
- Concurrency 32:
  - TTFT: p50=130 ms, p95=420 ms, p99=930 ms
  - Streaming per-token latency: p50=14 ms, p95=36 ms, p99=110 ms
  - Aggregate throughput: ~2.6k tokens/sec
- Concurrency 128 (stress run):
  - TTFT: p50=210 ms, p95=880 ms, p99=1.22 s (tail spikes observed)
  - Streaming per-token latency: p50=28 ms, p95=95 ms, p99=350 ms
  - Aggregate throughput: ~8.9k tokens/sec (GPU saturation observed)

Observations and next steps:
- For your pilot target (~20 concurrent sessions) we expect TTFT p95 in the 300–450 ms window based on interpolation; this meets your relaxed acceptance of 350ms only for some runs — we recommend the following mitigations to tighten tail: 
  1) Reduce autoscaling target burst size and increase headroom for quick prefix responses.
  2) Enable lightweight request-level batching cap (batch size cap = 8) for medium prompts to reduce kernel dispatch overhead.
  3) Use quantized fallback (mq8_compat) for low-cost emergency paths; will reduce p99 spikes at high concurrency with modest quality tradeoff.

- We also captured kernel-level traces for the worst p99 traces (attached IDs in CSV) and will share a short diff of runtime config changes we tested.

Attachments: streaming-results.csv

Happy to walk through these numbers on Monday's review.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
